items.description: Sec. 4 says 'See Figure 9 for domain sizes', and the text itself gives no dimensions. Table 2 (60×30, h_c=1/30), Table 3 (240×120, 1/120) and App. A (120×60, 1/60) all point to a 2×1 rectangle, if the first number is the horizontal count. The length L used for the load line (L/10) is defined only in the figure.
readings: 2 (horizontal) × 1 (vertical) rectangle, i.e. 2L × L with L = 1 = height
Same 2 × 1 rectangle labelled L × L/2, i.e. L = 2 = length (only the L-based quantities change)

items.description: The text never says where the Michell cantilever is supported. Sec. 4 points to Fig. 9 for the 'exact placement of boundaries', and Fig. 3a ('Cantilever beam with boundary conditions') is also unavailable. The name only suggests a support on the left side.
readings: Entire left edge x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H
Circular support region at mid-height near the left side (Michell's classical cantilever)
Only a central part of the left edge (e.g. 0.25H–0.75H)

items.description: The text does not say whether the support is clamped, pinned or a roller. This is shown only in Fig. 9.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all support nodes
Pinned only at the two end points (corners) of the left edge
u_x = 0 along the edge plus u_y = 0 at a single node

items.description: Sec. 4 says 'the force is applied along a line of 1/10 L in the Michell cantilever case' but does not give the edge, the position along it, or the line's orientation. These are in Fig. 9 only.
readings: Vertical segment on the right edge centred at mid-height (y = 0.5H)
Segment on the right edge at the bottom corner (y from 0 to L/10)
Segment on the right edge at the top corner

items.description: The text never states the load direction. It is shown only in Fig. 9.
readings: Vertical downward (−y), transverse to the beam axis
Vertical upward (+y): mirror-image layout, same compliance

items.description: No force value is given anywhere. The reported compliances C_ref and C_f (e.g. 106.21, 68.58) depend on it.
readings: Total force F = 1 spread over the line
Traction of 1 per unit length (total 0.1 or 0.2)

items.description: Sec. 4 gives the line length as L/10, but L is defined only in Fig. 9. With the 2×1 domain implied by Table 2, L could be the height or the length.

0.2 (L = length = 2): 6 elements on 60×30, 24 on 240×120

readings: Uniform traction with consistent nodal forces (end nodes at half weight)
Equal nodal forces on all nodes of the segment

items.description: Sec. 4 says elements 'in a small radius around the load are set to solid' but gives no radius.
readings: r ≈ 0.05 (half the load-line length, L/20 with L = 1)
r ≈ 0.1 (≈3 coarse elements on 60×30)
r ≈ 2 coarse elements (≈0.067)

items.entity: Rule 'elements with ρ>0.99 and in a small radius around the load are set to solid'
items.description: The Sec. 4 sentence can be read several ways. It may define passive (non-design) elements during optimization, or it may post-process the converged homogenization result; V_ref values slightly above 0.25/0.40 hint at post-processing. It is also unclear whether 'ρ>0.99' applies across the whole domain or only inside the radius.
readings: Post-processing only, with no passive elements during optimization
Passive solid disc at the load enforced throughout the optimization
After optimization, all elements with ρ>0.99 anywhere set to 1, plus a solid disc at the load
After optimization, only elements with ρ>0.99 inside the radius set to 1

items.description: The captions of Figs. 10–12 say V = 0.25 / 0.40. Table 2 instead lists V_ref = 0.2535/0.2568/0.2614 and 0.4024/0.4080/0.4165, which change with μ_min; Table 3 and App. A give slightly different values again. In Eq. (1) the constraint acts on ρ^d, whose superscript is never defined, and V_max is never given as a number.
readings: 0.25 and 0.40 (nominal values from the captions)
0.25/0.40 applied to a dilated realization ρ^d, so the blueprint volume is lower

items.description: No Young's modulus is given. Sec. 2.1.1 only gives the relative void stiffness α_out = 1e-9.
readings: E = 1 (non-dimensional), E_min = 1e-9·E
A physical modulus (e.g. 210 GPa)

items.description: No Poisson's ratio is stated anywhere. It usually has a minor effect on the layout of an isotropic single-material design.
The text states neither plane stress vs. plane strain nor the out-of-plane thickness.
readings: Plane stress, unit thickness
Plane strain, unit thickness

items.description: Sec. 4 gives 'a filter radius of r_min = 1.2 for varying mesh sizes' with no unit, filter type or weighting; per Eq. (2) the filter acts on μ1, μ2 and s. A radius of 1.2 physical length units would exceed the domain height of 1, so element widths are likely. If so, the physical radius shrinks as the mesh is refined.
readings: Linear-hat density filter, R = 1.2 element widths on each mesh (0.04 / 0.02 / 0.01 physical at 60×30 / 120×60 / 240×120)
Sensitivity filter, R = 1.2 element widths
Helmholtz/PDE filter with radius 1.2 element widths
Physical radius fixed at 1.2·(1/30) = 0.04 for all meshes

items.entity: Projection / robust formulation (bar-tilde variables, superscripts k, d, e)
items.description: Eqs. (2)–(4) use projected variables and the superscripts k, d and e: the volume constraint is on ρ^d and the area penalty on s^e. The paper does not give the projection function, β, the thresholds η, any continuation, or which realization the compliance is computed on.
readings: No projection: filtered fields used directly
Single tanh Heaviside projection, η = 0.5, β continued up to ~32
Robust eroded/intermediate/dilated projection (e.g. η = 0.7/0.5/0.3), compliance on eroded/intermediate design, volume on dilated design

items.entity: Material interpolation for a single-material solver
items.description: The reference solutions use rank-2 laminates (μ1, μ2, θ), whose closed-form homogenized stiffness is only cited to [9] (Sec. 2.1). The paper gives no SIMP/RAMP penalization or other equivalent for a single-material density solver.
readings: SIMP p = 3, E_min = 1e-9·E
p = 1 (variable-thickness sheet, closest to the grey homogenization result)
Rank-2 laminate stiffness with μ_min = 0.05/0.10/0.20 bounds as in Eq. (1)

items.description: Eq. (1) divides the compliance by 'a reference compliance' C_ref that is never defined, and Tables 2–3 reuse the same symbol for the final homogenization compliance. Its value sets the relative weight of the Γ = 0.05 solid-area penalty.
readings: Compliance of the initial uniform design
Compliance of a preliminary solution without the Γ term
The tabulated final compliance (e.g. 106.21 / 68.58)

items.entity: Optimizer, initial design and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 4 only says Eq. (1) is 'solved until convergence'. The optimizer, move limits, tolerance, iteration cap and initial design (including the initial θ) are not given.
readings: MMA, stopping at max design change < 0.01 or after a fixed iteration cap
OC update (top88-style, move 0.2), starting from a uniform design at the target volume
Initial θ aligned with the principal stresses of the uniform design

items.description: The element type is not stated (bilinear Q4 is the usual assumption). Sec. 4.2 uses three homogenization meshes: 60×30 (Table 2), 120×60 (App. A) and 240×120 (Table 3). C_f is evaluated on fine meshes from 1440×720 to 5760×2880. The text does not say which resolution a single-material re-run should use. Because r_min is in element units, the choice also changes the physical length scale.
readings: 60×30 Q4 elements, h = 1/30
Fine single-scale mesh 1440×720 or 2400×1200 (h_c/24 or h_c/40), as used for C_f
